pageCache.pageTitle: Kingsnorth Primary School - OPaL Termly Newsletters
pageCache.text:
OPaL Termly Newsletters
We are very pleased with the following comments from our OPaL assessor:
"You have successfully achieved the prestigious OPAL Gold Award, scoring 54 out of 72 points during the final audit accreditation. The outdoor play space has been transformed from standard tarmac and limited grass areas into a rich landscape of play opportunities.
Your playtime is now so much more joyful for children and staff. It was delightful to hear how many children said something along the lines of, 'I love playtime; I can go anywhere I like and play with whatever I want - I don't need anything more!' Importantly, when asked about dynamic risk assessment, they all knew to check they were keeping themselves and their friends safe enough, and many could articulate what they do to make potentially risky areas safer.
I particularly loved speaking to the mix of children in the dens and tree climbing area and seeing children freely enjoy the water play in such exceptional hot weather! They were all having such a lovely playtime!
Transformational Impact - The implementation of the OPAL framework at Kingsnorth CE Primary School has created a noticeable shift in school culture. By replacing a culture of play restrictions with a proactive risk-benefit framework, children have developed greater resilience and independence. Conflict resolution is increasingly managed by the pupils themselves, resulting in fewer behavioural issues requiring intervention from senior leadership.
Conclusion - Kingsnorth Church of England Primary School has achieved a significant milestone in securing the OPAL Gold Award. This achievement stands as a testament to the hard work, structural planning, and shared vision of the entire school community. By recognising that play is an essential vehicle for child development, Kingsnorth has created an environment where children can safely test their limits, expand their imaginations and build lifelong social skills. The school's Christian vision and values of care and nurturing are seen as fully aligned with the OPAL philosophy, providing a practical setting where relationships are valued and strengthened. The leadership remains committed to protecting the financial and physical resources required to sustain this positive trajectory over the coming years.

Kingsnorth After School Club is now run by the school, offering a range of activities in a play led environment, including arts, crafts, role-play, cooking activities, indoor and outdoor games. The facility provides the community of Kingsnorth with a safe and secure space for children to play and socialise after school. The club is open from 3:15pm until 6:00pm each weekday (during school term time) at £11.00 per session. and for 5 weeks, from 8am till 6pm during the school holidays and school INSET Days. £30 for a full day / £20 for a half day. School Choir
We are very lucky to have so many children interested in joining the school choir.
This club is open to all pupils in Years 4-6, and we currently have over 40 children attending!
Children join Mrs Howard and Miss Tree after school, every Monday. The club finishes at 4:00.
If your child wishes to join the choir, please apply via the online link. You will receive a text with the link attached.
Every year around January/February time, we go to the 02 to join up with other schools for an amazing concert. The trip for choir members is free, however we do ask for a payment to cover the coach cost. Prices will be confirmed at the time of booking.
This is a late night as the coach normally returns back to school at around 11pm. Children are required to attend school the following day as a normal working day.
Parents are able to purchase tickets to this event. Also available to purchase are DVDs of the performance and T-shirts for the choir members.
A very exciting and a once in a lifetime event, singing live at the 02!

pageCache.pageTitle: Kingsnorth Primary School - Adverse Weather Guidance
pageCache.text:
Adverse Weather Guidance
If it is bad weather in the morning the children can be taken straight to the classroom door, no earlier than 8.40am, and the class teacher will be there ready to receive the class. In conditions such as this, we may need to restrict access around the school site and may encourage children to use the main school entrance rather than access via the playground. Please be advised that when the weather is inclement access around and leading to school may be hazardous, so please be careful and dress accordingly for the conditions.
Emergency/School Closure In the event of an emergency the school will contact parents as soon as possible through the school text messaging service. This is the case whether the emergency takes place within the school day, or after hours. Examples of such emergencies include snow closure, burst pipes, no water, fire, etc. In the event of an emergency leading to school closure parents can listen to BBC Radio Kent, Heart FM and KMFM Ashford for school closure listings. Alternatively sign up to www.kentclosures.co.uk to be updated by KCC to your computer, tablet or mobile.This is a service provided for the residents of Kent, keeping you up to date with school and other KCC building closures.This is where we will post information about any closures or status of the school first – please register and sign up!
Once a decision to close has been made we will notify parents via the Kent Closures website and through our Twitter feed (@KINGSCEP). Kent Closures - Find your school and register for alerts Search for your town or school to see your schools current status.
You can register to receive free email alerts from your school when they update their status. Or, you can register for SMS updates (charges apply) to receive a text message alert straight to your mobile phone in conjunction with the Kent Messenger Group. Please read SMS terms, conditions and charges. “Schools should, wherever possible, stay open in severe weather. They play a key role in their communities and by staying open help both their pupils and parents.” – Department for Education Emergency Childcare
Our aim as a school is to remain open, where appropriate. This may result in us opening for ‘emergency childcare’ only. By this we mean that if we can form a ‘skeleton staff’ at school, we can remain open for those children who can get to school and whose parents need to get to work. If this is to be the case, we will contact parents to let them know that we are open for ‘emergency childcare’ only. We always have to be mindful of our adult:child ratios. We will work with the children through a ‘suspended’ curriculum for these sessions to develop project learning. Other educational activities can be found below to keep children who are not in school, actively learning. Below is a list of websites that may be of use to you to ensure that your child’s learning does not suffer, even if the weather does. Please use this time to talk to your child/ren and to get outside and enjoy the snowy weather. You may use the time to do some extra reading with your child or to extend their home learning in readiness for a return to school.
Some useful websites:
www.bbc.co.uk/learning/subjects/childrens_learning.shtml
www.bbc.co.uk/schools/parents
www.bbc.co.uk/schools
www.primaryhomeworkhelp.co.uk Health and Safety It is essential that the school has an emergency telephone number for both parents and where possible contact details for a friend or relative. To improve communications of a less urgent nature we are happy to contact you via text or email. We ask that you inform the school of any changes in these details.

Message from the Executive Headteacher
- Welcome to our School -
On behalf of everyone associated with our school, please accept our warmest welcome to our website. We hope that you find it informative and easy to find your way around.
Our school strives to serve the community by providing an excellent education for all pupils, of all abilities and backgrounds. We are a Church Controlled primary school and, as such, work hard to preserve and develop our distinctive Christian character, liaising closely with the local church and Canterbury Diocese.
Parents play an especially vital part in school life and there are lots of opportunities to share in the fun.
The pictures and words on our website can only give a small glimpse of our work. The best way to get to know us is to come and visit! You will be warmly welcomed by pupils and staff alike.
We endeavour to keep this website as current as it can be, but as always, it is subject to change and amendment at any time.
We have converted to an academy (01 November 2015) through the Diocese of Canterbury Multi Academy Trust (Aquila). We took this decision to enable our school to have greater autonomy and have a greater say in how we are run now and in the future. Kingsnorth CE Primary school is proud to be an active member of Aquila. To find out more about the Trust, visit their website
We look forward to showing you around. Mr I Witts Executive Headteacher
